title.value: Stochastic Mirror Descent: Convergence Analysis and Adaptive Variants via the Mirror Stochastic Polyak Stepsize
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the focus of the paper, which is the stochastic mirror descent method and its adaptive variants using the proposed mirror stochastic Polyak stepsize.
title.quote: Stochastic Mirror Descent: Convergence Analysis and Adaptive Variants via the Mirror Stochastic Polyak Stepsize

extractions.description: The paper investigates the convergence of stochastic mirror descent (SMD) methods in optimization. It focuses on providing new convergence guarantees for SMD with constant and adaptive stepsizes, introduces a novel adaptive stepsize scheme called mirror stochastic Polyak stepsize (mSPS), and demonstrates its effectiveness through experiments. Convergence results are derived without assuming bounded gradient or variance, making the methods broadly applicable across various machine learning tasks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is the optimization of machine learning algorithms, specifically stochastic mirror descent and its convergence properties. While optimization techniques can indirectly support sustainable development by improving efficiency in various systems, the paper does not explicitly focus on climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our research focuses on providing a comprehensive analysis of stochastic mirror descent (SMD) methods in smooth and relatively smooth convex optimization settings.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on any specific climate or ecological sustainable development category. Its primary aim is to enhance the optimization techniques in machine learning, which may have indirect applications in various fields, including sustainable development, but these are not expressly covered.
primary_category.quote: The contributions center around the convergence analysis of SMD in relatively smooth and smooth convex optimization and the introduction of an adaptive stepsize scheme, not on specific climate applications.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development since the paper's main contribution is in mathematical optimization methods applicable broadly within machine learning, without direct ties to sustainable development themes.
secondary_categories.quote: Our results extend to various supervised learning tasks but do not have a direct emphasis on sustainable development.

primary_sub_category.justification: As the paper is not focused on sustainable development, there is no applicable sub-category related to climate or ecological themes.
primary_sub_category.quote: This work is fundamentally about improving convergence guarantees of SMD and does not delve into ecological or climate sub-categories.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: The algorithmic advancements presented are applicable to a wide array of machine learning problems, with no specific sub-category highlighted for sustainability.

applications.justification: The paper discusses improvements in the stochastic mirror descent method, which can optimize machine learning algorithms' performance and efficiency.
applications.quote: mSPS remains both practical and efficient for modern machine learning applications while inheriting the benefits of mirror descent.

applications.justification: The experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed mSPS method across various supervised learning tasks, implying potential improvements in these areas.
applications.quote: We complement our results with experiments across various supervised learning tasks and different instances of SMD, demonstrating the effectiveness of mSPS.

new_primary_category.quote: The paper focuses on convergence analysis and adaptive variants for stochastic mirror descent, fitting well within machine learning optimization rather than introducing a new sustainable development category.
